name: Famotidine
summary: H2-receptor antagonist providing rapid acid suppression with minimal drug interactions — a common choice for GERD and ulcer disease.
mechanism: Competitive antagonist at parietal-cell H2 receptors, reducing basal and stimulated gastric acid secretion.

dosing.adult: GERD: 20 mg twice daily or 40 mg once daily; maintenance: 20 mg once daily
dosing.renalAdjustment: CrCl < 50 mL/min: reduce dose or lengthen the dosing interval

safety.pregnancy: Widely used in pregnancy; no major teratogenicity demonstrated
safety.lactation: Excreted in breast milk; considered compatible
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to famotidine or other H2 blockers
warnings: Rare confusion, especially in elderly or ICU patients
Long-term acid suppression may increase B12 deficiency and fracture risk
Investigate alarm symptoms (bleeding, weight loss, dysphagia) before treating

clinicalPearls: Least CYP-interacting H2 blocker — preferred over cimetidine in polypharmacy
Fast onset makes it useful for breakthrough heartburn
good: Fast, effective acid suppression with minimal drug interactions
bad: Renal impairment without dose adjustment; long-term use without a clear indication
